dedupe_keys.name: tonga submarine cable cuts after the hunga tonga hunga ha apai eruption january 2022

description: This recovery case documents how the eruption of the Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai volcano on 15 January 2022 and the tsunami that followed cut both the Tonga Cable, the only international submarine cable linking Tonga to Fiji, and its domestic extension to the outer island groups, isolating the kingdom from the Internet and most international telephony. Volcanic flows shredded a stretch of about 80 km of cable into many pieces, moved one section by several kilometres and buried another under silt. Limited satellite capacity was used in the interim; the international cable was repaired by a cable ship on 22 February 2022, while the domestic cable to Ha'apai and Vava'u was restored only on 12 July 2023, about eighteen months later, after ordering, manufacturing and shipping about 108 km of new cable from France. Coverage: Tonga and its connection to Fiji, 2022 to 2023. Format and access: free news and trade-press articles, with further details in Emergency Telecommunications Cluster situation reports on ReliefWeb. Caveats: information comes from press and humanitarian reports, not an official investigation; there is no technical failure data. Simulation uses: a reference case for hazard exposure of submarine cables to volcanic and tsunami hazards, cascading loss of connectivity for a small island state, recovery and restoration planning, and emergency communications using satellite backup. Related records: the TeleGeography submarine cable map shows the cable, IODA and Cloudflare Radar recorded the loss of connectivity.
